steps.text: Mix the hot chocolate mix, cinnamon, and cayenne pepper together in a mug.

Pour the milk into a glass measuring cup; heat in microwave on High until it begins to boil, about 2 minutes. Slowly pour over the mixture in the mug, stirring with a small whisk as you pour. Enjoy immediately.

raw_recipe.headline: Mayan Hot Chocolate
raw_recipe.description: Cayenne pepper and cinnamon are added to instant hot chocolate mix to make this Mayan-style hot chocolate.
raw_recipe.name: Mayan Hot Chocolate

recipeInstructions.text: Mix the hot chocolate mix, cinnamon, and cayenne pepper together in a mug.

Pour the milk into a glass measuring cup; heat in microwave on High until it begins to boil, about 2 minutes. Slowly pour over the mixture in the mug, stirring with a small whisk as you pour. Enjoy immediately.

review.reviewBody: I've been putting cayenne and cinnamon in my hot chocolate for years, but one other thing I add that makes it even more wonderful is about 1/8-1/4 tsp of ginger powder. Trust me...it's so delicious! Also, I don't use instant hot chocolate. I use about a cup and a half of milk, 2 tbls of cocoa powder and 2 tbls of sugar. I whisk it all together, along with the spices, over the stove. Just till blended and hot (don't boil it).

My son and I made this and had mixed reviews. We'll try it again because we liked the flavour but found its richness made it unpalatable by the end of the mug. I'd up the milk to 1.5 cups. Despite adding a small amount of milk to the dry ingredients and stirring to ensure everything was dissolved, there were still lumps...I'd likely use a whisk and do it on the stove next time.

I just made this for small tea cup sized portions. I didn't have cocoa mix on hand so I used cocoa and sugar as follows (again this is for small china tea cups 1 serving) 1 full tea cup milk, 1 teaspoon cocoa powder, 1 pinch cinnamon, 1 pinch red chili powder heated on lowest setting over gas stove for about 2-3 minutes or until almost at a boil! It really does taste like some of the hot cocoa I had in Mexico... I tried abuelita expecting similar things and was disappointed, this is perfect. It has a robust complex flavor and goes well with marshmallow cream if you want a little extra sweetness. Whipped cream if you have it will be more complimenting.

Really good! I lowered the chocolate powder to 2 Tbs bc I don’t like it too sweet and went crazy with the cayenne powder! I also took another reviewers advise and added ginger (I like using what I already have). For food measure I also added about a teaspoon of “café de olla” coffee mix. OH I made mine with powdered milk. I don’t go through milk fast enough to buy some so I am experimenting with powdered milk.

I added a shot of espresso. Too much cinnamon for me. More like a 1/4 teaspoon would be better. I had some freshly opened cayenne so a pinch was nice and spicy. The older your pepper, the more you need. Don't recommend heating the milk to boiling point. It ruins the milk. I like to use almond milk for extra richness.

What a disappointment to think I was opening a recipe for Mayan hot chocolate! People may enjoy drinking this, but please give it another name. This is not even remotely Mayan hot chocolate. Mayan hot chocolate is more similar to drinking coffee than hot cocoa. Mayan hot chocolate is made with water, not milk. It’s made with minimally refined chocolate and very little if any sugar. It sometimes has ground almonds. About the only thing the recipe got right is putting in some chili.

This was a real treat! I used a tbsp of really good unsweetened cocoa powder and about 1 tsp superfine sugar in place of the prepared hot chocolate mix which made it even more delicious. I even used skim milk and it was rich, creamy and satisfying, perfect for warming up after playing in the snow! My daughter liked hers with just the cinnamon, and I probably went a little light on that in hers.

I used Starbucks dark hot chocolate and I prepared it by dissolving the hot cocoa in a shot of hot coffee and then added the cinnamon cayenne and a sprinkling of dryer ginger powder.i just eyeballed a the spices. I finished with some vanilla whipped cream. Amazing!! You'll be bored with regular packet hot cocoa for good!!

This was definitely spicy, and it became quite addictive while drinking. I only used 1/2 t of cinnamon; at first I thought that was too much, but I liked it the more I drank. My cocoa mix had milk in it, so I just used water.
Watching the movie, Chocolat, free on YT, and I stopped the film to make this. I had all of the ingredients. I used unsweetened cocoa powder and raw sugar to taste. Buēno.
I use cocoa and sugar instead of a mix. I use 1/8 teaspoon of cayenne pepper. Mayan hot chocolate is the best hot chocolate I've ever tasted.
This was a little spicy obviously but it was really delicious once I drank more! I loved it!
IT WAS NICE!!!

I followed the recipe to a tee. It tastes delicious! Thank you for sharing the recipe. I doubled it, for my 16 oz mug. I also made use of my daughter's latte gadget to preheat the milk and then used my mini-blender to mix in the spices. I don't use a microwave - so I used my ss-pot and heated it up. It was perfection! Got my girls to taste test for me - and they both smiled brightly. It's a hit! (I premix my own cocoa powder with stevia, so no additives, no sugar).

I made this for my husband, but I took a sip so I could give it a rating. I made it spicy and hot because I kept adding more cayenne. I couldn't taste it at first, but then the flavor/hot came through. Whew! I had to dilute it with milk to tame it a bit, but it was very good!
‘‘Twas good ;)

The spices transform regular hot chocolate into a delicious drink with a nice kick. I enjoyed this different version and topped it with whipped cream. I'll definitely make this again. Thanks for the recipe!
I made it exactly as the recipe said and it is amazing.
This is awesome!!!
I liked the spiciness of the hot chocolate and it is toe warming!!
